newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian stocks weaker, Texaco up on result.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian stocks weaker, Texaco up on result.

text.p: Trading on the Nigerian stock market was thin and quiet on Thursday, the first day of business this year, pushing the all-share index slightly lower to 6992.01 from 6992.10 on Tuesday, the last day of activity in 1996.
The slide was due to losses by key stocks and adjustment of the price of one stock for dividend payment, traders said.
Demand for oil shares was boosted as Texaco reported an increase in its nine-month result to end-September 1996.
The company posted a net profit of 376.9 million naira compared to 246.7 million naira in the nine months to end-September 1995. Impressed traders hiked its share price by 50 kobo to 34.00 naira.

Interest in leading high street banks firmed up on improved public perception. United Bank for Africa was 6.10 naira and Union Bank closed at 6.08 naira, up five 10 kobo and eight kobo, respectively. First Bank traded unchanged at 7.10 naira.
But Afribank dropped 15 kobo to 3.50 naira due to the large volumes on offer.
Chemical and Allied Products which reported a loss for the six months to end-June 1996 fell to 6.00 naira, down 10 kobo.
Surplus stock of conglomerates SCOA and UTC saw their prices drop by one kobo each to 2.31 naira and 89 kobo, respectively.
Stationery maker Thomas Wyatt fell eight kobo to 6.30 naira while construction firm Costain slumped three kobo to 1.90.
Union Dicon Salt shed 1.50 naira, closing at 42.30 naira on adjustment for dividend payment. But fellow food-sector share Cadbury fell five kobo to 21.40 naira.
Dealers said caution would rule the market until fiscal 1997 budget is released later this month.
